# dtcloud_lb_listener (Resource)

Manages a listener on a load balancer: the protocol and port it accepts connections on.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_lb_listener" "https" {
  lb_id         = dtcloud_lb.public.id
  name          = "https"
  protocol      = "HTTPS"
  protocol_port = 443

  # Only these addresses may reach the listener.
  allowed_cidrs = ["10.0.0.0/8"]

  # Milliseconds here. dtcloud_lb_balancing_pool takes the same three in seconds.
  timeout_client_data = 50000
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `lb_id` (String) ID of the load balancer this listener belongs to. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `protocol` (String) Front-end protocol. One of: HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, UDP. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `protocol_port` (Number) Front-end port the listener accepts traffic on. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `admin_state_up` (Boolean) Whether the listener is administratively up.
- `allowed_cidrs` (List of String) CIDRs permitted to reach this listener.
- `connection_limit` (Number) Maximum number of concurrent connections.
- `default_pool_id` (String) Pool that receives traffic when no other rule matches.
- `description` (String) Free-text description.
- `insert_headers` (Block List, Max: 1) Headers the listener injects into requests forwarded to members. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--insert_headers))
- `name` (String) Name of the listener.
- `timeout_client_data` (Number) Client inactivity timeout in milliseconds.
- `timeout_member_connect` (Number) Member connect timeout in milliseconds.
- `timeout_member_data` (Number) Member inactivity timeout in milliseconds.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp as reported by the API.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `listener_id` (String) ID of the listener on its own, without the load balancer prefix.
- `operating_status` (String) Operating status.
- `provisioning_status` (String) Provisioning status.
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp as reported by the API.

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **`protocol` and `protocol_port` are fixed at creation.** Everything else changes in place. The
  create call accepts only the protocol, the port, a name and a description, so the provider applies
  the rest in a second call right after.
* **The three timeouts are milliseconds here.** `dtcloud_lb_balancing_pool` takes the same three in
  seconds. The asymmetry is the API's: that endpoint converts, this one does not.
* **Left unset, the platform fills the timeouts and the connection limit in** and reports what it
  chose. They are Computed for that reason, so an omitted value does not read as a difference.
* **`allowed_cidrs` is answered as `null` when empty.** Only a non-empty list is written to state, so
  omitting the argument and the platform reporting nothing agree.

## Timeouts

`create`, `update` and `delete` each default to 15 minutes. Every call waits for the parent load
balancer to settle first.

## Import

```shell
# <load-balancer-id>:<listener-id>
terraform import dtcloud_lb_listener.https 3d372446-4c75-4327-9511-98442456162f:8c1f0b7a-22e5-4a90-b5d1-1f3c9e77a201
```

The id carries the load balancer, because every listener call is scoped to it and the listener id
alone cannot address one.
